prompt:
Minecraft builder reference sheet, landscape 3:2, plain light background, crisp vanilla Minecraft voxel style, no characters or animals. Two views side by side, LEFT straight-on north/front elevation orthographic, RIGHT three-quarter north-east view at the same block scale. Show the same entire house and lot in both views. Skilled human builder quality with substantial massing, projecting details, recessed framed openings, authentic stepped roof verges/eaves/ridges and sub-block stairs, slabs, fences, walls, trapdoors and lanterns.

Site: suburban McMansion seen from the street (north), 44 blocks wide x 32 deep, two storeys plus attic, 14 blocks tall to the highest entry ridge including lawn and driveway, flat cul-de-sac lot with manicured green lawn. Left: 18-wide three-car garage wing, beige birch siding over stone-veneer base, three 4-wide carriage-style doors built of spruce panels with glass windows above, separated by lantern posts, hipped dark-asphalt roof. Wide gray concrete driveway flares toward street. Centre: tall 10-wide gable-fronted entry, highest ridge of house, two-storey portico with FOUR white quartz columns, white pediment, double dark oak doors under fanlight, three stone steps from polished-andesite walk. Right of entry: round-ish polygonal turret bay in stone veneer, tall glass windows, conical stepped dark roof and rod finial. Main block behind: jumble of hipped dark deepslate-tile roofs with flat decks and TWO small gabled dormers. Big stone-brick chimney on right with TWO pots. Lower front stone veneer, upper beige birch siding, white trim, alternating corner quoins. Tall arched 3-wide windows with upside-down quartz stairs in top corners, black iron shutters. Foundation shrubs of leaves and azalea along front wall, young oak with oak fence stake near driveway. Back: spruce deck with fence rail and sliding glass door, visible where possible in right view. Use only vanilla blocks. Do not introduce other materials.

Exact block palette by role:

plinth: cobblestone
beige siding: birch_planks, birch_stairs, birch_slab, birch_fence

roof asphalt: deepslate_tiles, deepslate_tile_stairs, deepslate_tile_slab, deepslate_tile_wall
shutters: iron_trapdoor, dark_oak_trapdoor
windows: glass_pane, white_stained_glass_pane, glass
doors: dark_oak_door, spruce_door, birch_door

driveway: gray_concrete, polished_andesite_slab
path: polished_andesite

shrubs: oak_leaves, flowering_azalea_leaves
tree: oak_log, oak_leaves, oak_fence
deck: spruce_planks, spruce_stairs, spruce_fence, spruce_slab

flowers: rose_bush, peony, lilac, allium, cornflower
functional/decor objects: lightning_rod, iron_bars.
Include small unobtrusive view captions FRONT / THREE-QUARTER and dimension guides 44 x 32 / height 14. Prioritize the architecture and readable block textures over text. Constraints: no characters or animals.
changes: Saved the generated image without post-processing as concept.png in the current directory.

Block ids are visual interpretations of raster concept art, not verified world data. The roles retain every planned block; some planned blocks are hidden or not visibly distinguishable. Small flowers, sidewalk material, chimney-pot construction and fine ironwork are especially uncertain.
The entry gable is substantially lower than the main roof, turret finial and chimney; it is not the highest ridge.
The portico reads as two broad column groups rather than four clearly separated columns.
The front view reveals roof tops and ground depth, so it is not a strict orthographic front elevation. Identical block scale between views is not verifiable.
The dimension labels state 44 by 32 by 14, but exact block counts, garage width, entry width and window widths cannot be established from the drawing.
The shutters appear brown dark-oak trapdoors rather than black iron shutters.
The fanlight and some window arches use curved or fine radial details that do not correspond cleanly to vanilla block geometry.
Garage panels resemble oversized custom carriage doors; their exact vanilla spruce-block assembly is ambiguous.
The rear deck becomes a raised balcony with a fenced ground-level area and extensive glazing below. A distinct sliding glass door is not identifiable.
The young oak has a surrounding fence enclosure rather than a single stake. Additional trees appear beside or behind the house.
Landscaping is more elaborate, with extra flower beds, yellow flowers interpreted as dandelion, grass tufts and numerous lantern-topped path posts.
The chimney has reddish brick pots, adding bricks and brick_wall to the planned palette.
A pale sidewalk and curb are added, interpreted as smooth_stone and smooth_stone_slab. A straight street strip is shown rather than a recognizable cul-de-sac.
The driveway is mostly rectangular rather than visibly flaring toward the street.
The two views differ in small landscaping and deck details. Interior floor materials, birch_door, spruce_door and end_rod are not visibly confirmed.
